faq.q: What is the Income Tax Act, 2025?
faq.a: The Income Tax Act, 2025, is a new law that replaced the Income Tax Act, 1961, from April 1, 2026. Its main goal is to simplify, streamline, and modernize India's direct tax code, making it more taxpayer-friendly and reducing compliance burdens.

faq.q: When do these new penalty rules come into effect?
faq.a: The changes to penalty and prosecution provisions are part of the Income Tax Act, 2025, and Income Tax Rules, 2026, which are effective from April 1, 2026, for the Tax Year 2026-27 onwards. Specific provisions, like the merger of penalty proceedings with assessment, apply to assessments/reassessments made on or after April 1, 2027.

faq.q: What does "misreporting of income" mean in this context?
faq.a: Misreporting of income generally refers to instances where a taxpayer furnishes inaccurate particulars of income or conceals income, leading to a lower tax liability. The new rules offer immunity under specific conditions if the taxpayer pays the due tax, interest, and an additional tax.

faq.q: Will these changes reduce tax litigation in India?
faq.a: Yes, one of the stated objectives of these reforms, including the changes to penalty provisions, is to reduce tax litigation. By providing clearer guidelines, offering immunity for minor errors, and streamlining processes, the government aims to decrease the number of disputes between taxpayers and the tax department.

faq.q: Does this apply to all types of taxpayers?
faq.a: These changes generally apply to all taxpayers, including individuals, businesses, and other entities, who are subject to the Income Tax Act, 2025. The aim is to make the tax system more equitable and predictable for everyone.
